chapter: Mandeville, Bunk Johnson and society banquets
title: Reading music in Mandeville bands; Zeb, Edmund Hall and clarinet tone
summary: George says few bands there used music, names the clarinetist Zeb, and compares clarinet tones with Edmund Hall and Georgie Boyd.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well what about the Fritz band? Bunk was instructing them you said? Did they play it before they learned how to read or what? Well I never saw anyone with any music. I'm not telling you. I don't know. Well how did Bunk instruct him then?
Bunk was teaching them, that's all I see.

I never saw any music. I never saw no band use any music except, the first band I saw use music over there was Leonard Parker's band. And then Parker was a good spell a little bit and he used to, I saw him with music. But the rest of them I never saw anyone with no music. And then also René used to come over there with Morris French and Morris French's brother with the tuba, playing the tuba at the different time, used to come over there and they wrote it.
Zeb. Zeb. Zeb was playing the clarinet.
What style did Zeb play, interrupt again? What kind of a player was Zeb?
Zeb played on the style I played on almost. Just not one part of the same style.
Did you hear Edmund Hall over there?
Yes. I tried to take Edmund Hall, plays with Buddy Petit when Edmund Hall left.
Did he play the same as he plays now? Almost. Almost. Would Zeb have a tone like him or more like yours? Zeb had a tone more like Edmund Hall. What about Georgie Boyd? What kind of tone did he have?
Georgie Boyd had a tone like Edmund Hall too.
